entries.title: Mark 5:9
segments: My name is Legion. The word 'Legion' is used because it expressed the popular idea of great numbers.  In the New Testament period a Roman legion included ten cohorts of six centuries each.  A cohort contained six hundred men; a century, one hundred men.

entries.title: Mark 5:11
segments: A great herd of swine feeding. As swine were an abomination to the Jews, the fact that there was such a herd at large suggests the wild and uncivilized nature of the district.

entries.title: Mark 5:17
segments: To depart from their borders. Probably among those who besought him to depart were the owners of the swine, who were troubled over their loss.

entries.title: Mark 5:18
segments: Besought him that he might be with him. This appeal of the man who was now restored to reason was unspeakably pathetic.  No wonder that he wished to be with his divine Deliverer.

entries.title: Mark 5:25
segments: A woman, who had an issue of blood twelve years. While Jesus was on his way to the bedside of the daughter of Jairus, he was timidly approached by this woman, whose meekness and modesty would not permit her to press forward boldly toward him.  Her touch of humble, quiet faith contrasts with the crowding of the throng.

entries.title: Mark 5:36
segments: Fear not, only believe In his miracles our Lord insists with tremendous force upon the necessity of faith for those who would be healed.  So here he ignores the report of the death of the ruler's little daughter and turns to the ruler himself, concerned only about the latter's faith.

entries.title: Mark 5:42
segments: They were amazed straightway. The word 'amazed' here expresses an almost helpless wonder.  It was a wholesome reaction from the jeering scorn and doubt with which they had at first greeted our Lord.
